fields.meta_title: Event Landing Page Builder With Guest Lists | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an event landing page with a guest list you own, check-in at the door and a headcount that counts every plus-one against the venue limit.
fields.h1: Build an Event Landing Page That Fills the Room
fields.hero_description: Describe the event and who should come. Emergent builds the event landing page and its registration form, plus a guest list you own that your team checks people in from.
fields.features_heading: What Event Landing Pages Do After Sign-Up
fields.features_subheading: Most layouts stop at the register button. An event page keeps working until the doors close, in the guest list and at check-in.
fields.feature_1:
Venue address with a directions link

The venue address sits above the fold, next to the date and the hour the doors open. A directions link opens Google Maps on that address, and the confirmation email carries it too.
fields.feature_2:
Questions the venue needs answered

Ask for a dietary need or an access request on the form. Each answer saves to its own column, and the totals by type are ready to send to the caterer or the crew setting up the room.
fields.feature_3:
Check-in from the guest list

On the day, volunteers find each guest by name on a tablet and tap Check In. Every arrival saves with a timestamp, and the organizer sees how many people are inside at any hour.
fields.feature_4:
Headcount against the room limit

Set the capacity of the room, and the page counts every registration, plus-ones included, against it. Once the count reaches the limit, a waitlist takes the place of the form.
fields.feature_5:
Venue changes made by message

Tell Emergent the event moved across town, and the page and its directions link change with it, markup included. Everyone already registered gets an email with the new address.
fields.feature_6:
The event site in your own repository

Emergent exports the page and its guest list table to your GitHub on paid plans. Run it on Emergent under your custom domain, or deploy the code to hosting your team already runs.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Events, Four Different Guest Lists
fields.tab_content_1:
Every diet in the lunch order, counted per day

Ridgeline's operations summit runs two days in Portland, and its registration form asks each attendee for one dietary need. The venue coordinator gets an email 72 hours before doors open with the lunch count for the first day: 340 meals, 72 of them special, each type listed with its number.
fields.tab_content_2:
Gate check-in on a tablet, tallied hourly

On market night, Harbor Street's volunteers stand at the gate with tablets. They search each name from the 1,240 free RSVPs and tap Check In, and every arrival saves with its time. By 9 PM, the organizers' dashboard shows 812 people through the gate, with 7 PM the busiest hour.
fields.tab_content_3:
Plus-ones added to one running headcount

Guests invited to Copperline Studio's 10th anniversary party RSVP on a private page, and each can bring a guest. The headcount counts every plus-one against the venue's limit of 150. With 96 guests saying yes and 31 bringing someone, it stands at 127 of 150, and the form closes when it hits the limit.
fields.tab_content_4:
Four cities and four reps behind one page

One page carries every stop of the Tallgrass Analytics breakfast roadshow, and a visitor picks a city on the form. The registration lands in HubSpot with that city's rep as owner, and the rep gets a direct message in Slack. Austin sign-ups go to Dana Whitfield.

fields.howto_title: How to Build an Event Landing Page
fields.howto_description: An event page asks people to show up somewhere at a set time. These steps start with the details guests look for first and end with the numbers you need on the day.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Lead with the date and the venue
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Name the audience and the program
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask only what the day depends on
fields.howto_step_1_des: Visitors decide in seconds whether they can come. Put the weekday and the date beside the headline, with the city underneath. Someone who has to scroll to find out where the event happens will usually leave before reaching the form.
fields.howto_step_2_des: A subhead such as for operations leads at companies with one warehouse sorts the room before anyone registers. Below it, list the sessions or acts with start times. A conference needs the full agenda; a party needs one line about the night.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Link the address to Google Maps with a Maps URL, which needs the api=1 parameter to open on the venue. Then add the nearest transit stop, where to park and whether the entrance has step-free access for wheelchairs and strollers.
fields.howto_step_4_des: A name and an email confirm a place. Add a field only when someone acts on the answer: a dietary need tells the caterer what to cook, and a plus-one changes the headcount. Every extra question costs you some registrations.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Mark up the event for search
fields.howto_step_5_des: Google's Event structured data describes a physical event with a Place location and a full PostalAddress. If the date moves, set eventStatus to EventRescheduled and add previousStartDate, which tells search engines the old date no longer holds.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Event links travel through group chats and social posts. The og:title and og:image tags decide what a shared link shows. Use an image with the date and city in large type, readable at the size of a phone thumbnail.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Plan check-in before the doors open
fields.howto_step_7_des: Volunteers at the door need a list sorted by last name, with a button that marks each arrival. Timestamps show when the line peaked and how many registrants never came, which sets the overbooking margin for your next event.

plan.angle: The top 10 for this term are design galleries (Dribbble, Pinterest), example roundups (Unbounce, OptimizePress, ConvertFlow), a HubSpot template marketplace, an event platform guide (Splash) and a university design system. They judge an event page by its layout and stop at the register button. This page defines the term for the AI Overview, then shows four in-person event formats with what the registrations do after the click: a catering count by dietary need for a conference, gate check-in for a free street market, a party headcount that counts plus-ones against the venue limit, and a city roadshow that hands each sign-up to that city's rep. The how-to covers venue details, directions, the share preview and Google's Event markup for a physical place.
tab_stories: Ridgeline's two-day operations summit asks every registrant for a dietary need, and 72 hours before doors the venue coordinator receives a lunch count of 340 with the 72 special meals listed by type.

Harbor Street Night Market takes free RSVPs on its page, and on the night volunteers at the gate search each name on a tablet and tap Check In, so the organizers watch 812 of 1,240 RSVPs arrive hour by hour.
Copperline Studio's invite-only tenth anniversary party lets each guest add a plus-one on the RSVP form, and the headcount counts every plus-one against the venue's 150-person limit.
Tallgrass Analytics runs one breakfast roadshow page for four cities, and each sign-up goes to HubSpot with that city's rep as owner, who also gets a direct message in Slack.
